title: Reduction and numerical stability: row softmax

steps.title: Three-pass softmax: shared memory tree reduction
Online softmax: (m, l) in one pass
Keep the whole row in registers: float4, one warp/block per row

cases.name: tiny
cases.purpose: Slightly wider than a warp: the column count is not a multiple of 4 or 32; checks tail handling and -inf padding.

cases.name: one_col
cases.purpose: cols = 1: each row's output is exactly 1; most threads get no element, so this checks handling of the empty state (m = -inf, l = 0).

cases.name: one_row
cases.purpose: rows = 1: the grid has only one block; 1000 is a multiple of 4 but not of 32 or 128.

cases.name: tail
cases.purpose: Odd column count: float4 cannot be used, so the scalar path runs; threads get uneven element counts.

cases.name: short_rows
cases.purpose: Many short rows, and the row count is not a multiple of rows per block: checks the bounds check of the last block in the warp-per-row configuration.

cases.name: wide
cases.purpose: Very wide rows (128 KB): step 4 uses the largest register configuration, 32 elements per thread.

cases.name: huge_row
cases.purpose: A row does not fit in registers: step 4 must fall back to the online version; odd column count.

cases.name: large
cases.purpose: |x| reaches several thousand: without first subtracting the row maximum, exp overflows to inf and the result becomes NaN.

cases.name: shifted
cases.purpose: Adds 5000 to each row, which leaves softmax unchanged: checks the precision of computing x - m first and then multiplying by log2(e).

cases.name: constant
cases.purpose: Every element of a row is the same: the output is all 1/cols; checks the accumulation of l and the normalization.

cases.name: masked
cases.purpose: About half the elements are -inf (as after a causal mask): checks that (-inf) - (-inf) = NaN is avoided.

cases.name: masked_short
cases.purpose: Short rows with -inf: some threads get only -inf, so their local maximum is -inf.

cases.name: medium
cases.purpose: Medium-size random data with the same column count as the first perf case.

cases.name: rows4096
cases.purpose: 256 MB input (larger than the 126 MB L2), medium row width: 16 KB per row, one block per row.

cases.name: rows32768
cases.purpose: 512 MB input, wide rows: 128 KB per row; checks bandwidth with 32 register elements per thread.

cases.name: rows256
cases.purpose: 256 MB input, many short rows: one warp per row; checks bandwidth on short rows.
